draft.title: The Hundred Flowers Campaign
card: In 1956 and 1957 Mao Zedong invited people to speak out. The slogan said to let a hundred flowers bloom and a hundred schools of thought contend.
At first few people responded. By May 1957 many intellectuals, teachers and students were criticising the Communist Party and its officials.
The criticism went further than Mao had expected. Some people questioned the Party's right to rule.
From mid-1957 the Anti-Rightist Campaign targeted those labelled rightists. Many critics lost their jobs, were sent to labour camps or were sent to work in the countryside.
draft.remember: Mao invited criticism, then punished many who gave it.

a.q: What happened to many of the people who criticised the Party during the Hundred Flowers Campaign?
opts: They were labelled rightists and punished
They were given posts in the Party leadership
They were praised and their ideas became policy
They were ignored and faced no consequences
a.why: After the criticism grew, the Anti-Rightist Campaign targeted those who had spoken out, and many lost jobs or were sent to labour camps. Being ignored is tempting, but the Party acted against critics.
a.clue: What followed the campaign in mid-1957?

b.q: Lin is a university lecturer in Beijing. In May 1957 she publicly criticises local Party officials, as Mao had invited. What is most likely to happen to her later in 1957?
opts: She is labelled a rightist and loses her job
She is promoted for being honest and loyal
She is protected because Mao asked for criticism
She is asked to lead a new Party committee
b.why: Many intellectuals who spoke out were targeted in the Anti-Rightist Campaign, so Lin is likely to be labelled a rightist and lose her job. Mao's invitation is the tempting reason for safety, but the campaign turned on those who had accepted it.
b.clue: Think about what came after the criticism grew.

a.best: They were labelled rightists and punished

b.best: She is labelled a rightist and loses her job

check.summary: No problems found. The card is accurate on the Hundred Flowers and Anti-Rightist campaigns, and both questions have one clear answer that matches the explanations.
